q-16442.name: Question 1
q-16442.worked_solution:
The denominator is $3+10\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $3-10\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $3-10\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{3+10\text{i}} & =\frac{6}{3+10\text{i}}\cdot \frac{3-10\text{i}}{3-10\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{9-30\text{i}+30\text{i}-{10}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{9-100{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{9-100(-1)} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{9+100} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{109}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{18-60\text{i}}{109}=\frac{18}{109}-\frac{60}{109}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-74641.name: Question 2
q-74641.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-4+3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-4-3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-4-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{8\text{i}}{-4+3\text{i}} & =\frac{8\text{i}}{-4+3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-4-3\text{i}}{-4-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-32\text{i}-24{\text{i}}^{2}}{(-4)^{2}-{3}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-32\text{i}-24(-1)}{(-4)^{2}-{3}^{2}(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-32\text{i}+24}{16+9} \\  & =\frac{24-32\text{i}}{25}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{24-32\text{i}}{25}=\frac{24}{25}-\frac{32}{25}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

,8i−4+3i=

a
 3225−2425i
b
 2425−3225i
c
 −2425−3225i
d
 −2425+3225i
e
 1425−3225i

Correct
EXPLANATION

The denominator is −4+3i and its conjugate is −4−3i. We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by −4−3i, so that the denominator turns into a real number:

,8i−4+3i=,8i−4+3i⋅−4−3i−4−3i=−32i−24i2(−4)2−32i2=−32i−24(−1)(−4)2−32(−1)=−32i+2416+9=24−32i25

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form a+bi:

24−32i25=2425−3225i

q-74657.name: Question 3
q-74657.worked_solution:
Here, the denominator is the imaginary number $10\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+10\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-10\text{i},$ or simply $-10\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-10\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-7+6\text{i}}{10\text{i}} & =\frac{-7+6\text{i}}{10\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-10\text{i}}{-10\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{70\text{i}-60{\text{i}}^{2}}{-100{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{70\text{i}-60(-1)}{-100(-1)} \\  & =\frac{60+70\text{i}}{100}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{60+70\text{i}}{100} & =\frac{60}{100}+\frac{70}{100}\text{i} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}+\frac{7}{10}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by −10i, so that the denominator turns into a real number:

−7+6i10i=−7+6i10i⋅−10i−10i=70i−60i2−100i2=70i−60(−1)−100(−1)=60+70i100

60+70i100=60100+70100i=35+710i
